# Frame TV Art Manager

Frame TV Art Manager is a noncommercial source-available Go service for NAS and home-server owners who want to prepare and synchronize personal artwork with one or more Samsung Frame TVs over a local network.

Last substantive update: 2026-07-26
Maintainer: MikeO7 — https://github.com/MikeO7
Canonical website: https://mikeo7.github.io/frame-tv-art-manager/
Source repository: https://github.com/MikeO7/frame-tv-art-manager
License: PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0; commercial use is not permitted by the current license.
Affiliation: independent software; not affiliated with or endorsed by Samsung.

## Intended use

- Maintain a local JPEG and PNG artwork collection on Samsung Frame TVs.
- Run continuously with Docker Compose or as a compiled Go binary.
- Replace repeated phone uploads when a folder changes often or multiple TVs use the same collection.
- Target Samsung Frame hardware running Tizen 8.0 or newer. Other firmware may work but is not the primary target.

## Minimal operation

- Required environment variable: one or more TV addresses in `TV_IPS`.
- Operational prerequisites: persistent `/data` storage, a stable TV address, LAN reachability, and one approval on the television.
- The first synchronization cycle starts with the service. Later cycles default to every 30 minutes.
- Multiple TVs are supported through a comma-separated `TV_IPS` list.

## Artwork and image defaults

- Accepted local and upload formats: JPEG and PNG.
- Image optimization is enabled by default.
- Default output dimensions: 3840 by 2160 pixels; dimensions are configurable.
- Smart crop and museum treatment are optional and disabled by default.
- Portrait images can be cropped, padded, or combined into landscape collages.

## Network behavior

- TV synchronization communicates directly over the LAN using Samsung's private Art Mode protocol.
- A local-only collection does not require SmartThings or a Samsung cloud account.
- Configured remote artwork providers contact their external APIs.
- The optional HTTP smart-crop provider may receive a maximum-512-pixel JPEG preview at an operator-configured URL.
- The authenticated upload endpoint is disabled by default. Plain HTTP Basic authentication should remain on a trusted LAN or behind TLS.

## Retention and deletion behavior

- Unknown or unowned TV artwork is preserved unless `REMOVE_UNKNOWN_IMAGES=true` is explicitly enabled.
- The artwork currently selected on the TV is preserved.
- An empty desired collection preserves the final known-good manager-owned item under the default policy.
- Removing a remote source does not automatically delete files it previously downloaded; downloaded files remain local until the operator removes them.
- Incomplete collection or TV observations cannot authorize destructive changes.
- Dry-run mode does not pair, persist tokens, wake a TV, upload, delete, or change the display.
